questions.q: What should drive MySQL backup tool choice, per this lesson?
options: Whatever the previous DBA happened to use, without reassessment
Whichever tool is installed by default on the server
The DBA's personal preference for command-line tools
RPO and RTO targets, defined first, before picking specific tools
questions.explain: Recovery Point Objective and Recovery Time Objective should be defined first and drive which tools and cadence actually meet them.

questions.q: For a large, high-write production MySQL database, what combination does this lesson describe as a realistic DR plan?
options: Binary logs alone, with no full backup ever taken
Manually copying individual rows via SELECT statements
A single mysqldump taken once a year
Periodic full XtraBackup, daily incrementals, and continuous binary logging for point-in-time precision
questions.explain: For large databases, a full XtraBackup plus incrementals gives fast restores, while binlogs add point-in-time precision on top.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say local-server-only backup copies aren't true disaster recovery?
options: Local backups are always corrupted
MySQL cannot write backup files to local disk
They don't protect against the server itself failing or being lost entirely — off-server/off-site copies are needed
Local backups take longer to create than remote ones
questions.explain: Backups stored only on the same server protect against accidents but not against loss of the server itself, which is the disaster recovery scenario.

questions.q: What does this lesson say makes a backup plan a genuine, working recovery capability rather than a plan on paper?
options: Having the backup script committed to source control
Storing the backup in multiple file formats
Actually restoring the backup to a separate environment, verifying the data, and timing it against the RTO
Scheduling the backup to run nightly, regardless of whether it's ever restored
questions.explain: An untested backup isn't a real backup — a genuine test means exercising the restore path and measuring real recovery time.

questions.q: What does the outro of this lesson say comes next in Chapter Ten?
options: A second course on Oracle disaster recovery
MySQL performance tuning methodology, applying the same measure, identify, change, verify discipline
A repeat of the logical vs. physical backup comparison
Directly configuring MySQL replication with no further backup discussion
questions.explain: The lesson closes Chapter Nine and transitions into Chapter Ten's opening lesson on MySQL performance tuning methodology.
